subject: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations
related_links: Linear: ENG-4829 (Private installer compatibility for LTS)
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

Connor —

We’re finalizing the Private installer docs updates for the LTS pilot, but we’re blocked on a couple versioning / artifact location details.

Can you confirm the intended semantics so we can write unambiguous upgrade guidance?

1) Version format:
- Are we standardizing on `runtime-1.20-lts.0`, `runtime-1.20-lts.1`, etc (note the dot before patch), or `runtime-1.20-lts-0` style?
- Does the “.0” correspond to the initial branch cut (i.e., first supported LTS release), or can we ship a “.0” later after a short RC period?

2) Artifact references for Private:
- Do we want Private to pin to an image tag (e.g. `ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:1.20-lts.1`) or a signed manifest that resolves to an immutable digest?
- Are we expecting customers to use a channel label (`1.20-lts`) that moves, or only explicit patch tags?

3) Supported upgrade paths (what we’ll document):
- Can customers go from `1.20-lts.0` -> `1.20-lts.2` skipping patches? (I’d like to say “yes” if the backport policy + testing is consistent.)
- Any supported path from standard train -> LTS (e.g. `1.21.3` -> `1.20-lts.1`)? My gut says we should discourage “downshifts” unless it’s a rollback and we call it out.

4) Rollback language (compliance):
- Naomi flagged that we should avoid promising “no behavior change” and instead use “no known breaking changes; changes documented; rollback supported if within X window.” Can you share the exact LTS guarantee language you’re using?

I can sync our doc draft to your release notes template once I have these answers.

Thanks,
Vivek

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference


Attachment: Private_LTS_upgrade_matrix_v0.1.xlsx


From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 10:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

Good questions — we’ve been tightening this up this week.

1) Version format
We’re standardizing on:
- Branch: `runtime-1.20-lts`
- Releases: `runtime-1.20-lts.0`, `runtime-1.20-lts.1`, ...
- Container tags: `1.20-lts.0`, `1.20-lts.1` (no `runtime-` prefix in the tag)

“.0” = first GA LTS patch off the branch cut. We might cut RCs as `1.20-lts.0-rc1` etc but we won’t tell customers to deploy RCs unless they opt into it.

2) Artifact references
For Private, we should document:
- Customers pin to explicit patch tags (e.g. `1.20-lts.1`) OR (recommended) pin by digest.
- We will also publish signed provenance (attestation) and checksums. Sahana is wiring the “digest + attestation” story into the promotion job.

We do NOT want a moving `1.20-lts` tag. Too easy to silently drift.

3) Supported upgrade paths
- Yes, skipping patches should be supported within the same LTS line: `1.20-lts.0` -> `1.20-lts.2`.
- Standard train -> LTS: we should frame this as a migration that must be validated. I’d avoid saying it’s “supported” unless we explicitly test it. It’s effectively a downgrade across minor, and we can’t guarantee config compatibility.

4) Guarantee language
Agree with Naomi. The phrase we’ve been using in drafts is:
“LTS releases prioritize stability. Changes are limited to security fixes, correctness fixes, and narrowly scoped performance/stability improvements. No intentional breaking changes; any behavior changes are documented in the LTS release notes with risk level and mitigations.”

Sahana may have more concrete wording once we finalize the provenance docs.

If helpful, I can also add a short section to the Private upgrade guide: “How to verify you’re running exactly the artifact we shipped” (tag -> digest -> attestation).

-Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 10:24 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

Adding a bit more on the artifact piece since it’s easy to get inconsistent between docs + installer.

What we can support in the pilot:
- Installer takes either `--runtime-image-tag 1.20-lts.1` OR `--runtime-image-digest sha256:...`
- If tag is provided, installer resolves tag -> digest and writes the resolved digest into the install state so re-runs are deterministic.
- We publish:
  - image digest
  - SBOM
  - SLSA-ish provenance attestation (we’re using Sigstore/cosign)
  - checksums file for offline mirror use

Docs suggestion (to avoid promising more than we do):
- “Pin to patch tag for convenience; for strict environments pin by digest and verify attestation.”

We should avoid the word “immutable tag” (it’s true in spirit, but ops teams will ask what enforces it).

Also: for air-gapped / on-prem, we’ll provide a manifest file per patch with all digests so they can mirror.

Sahana

—
Sahana Iyer
CI/Build Automation
Redwood Inference


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 11:08 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

+1 to the above.

On language: for compliance we should be explicit about what customers can rely on vs what is “best effort.”

Suggested phrasing for the Private guide:
- “No intentional breaking changes within an LTS line.”
- “Behavior changes may occur as part of correctness/security fixes; these are documented.”
- “Customers should validate upgrades in a staging environment and canary production per their change-management policy.”

Also, please avoid:
- “backwards compatible” (too broad)
- “audit-ready by default” (we can say “includes provenance and traceability artifacts”) 

If we reference attestations/SBOMs, we should link to the exact location and note retention window (we should align to whatever we’re committing in the enterprise PRD).

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Compliance Requirements (Enterprise Readiness)
Redwood Inference


From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 12:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

This is helpful, thanks all.

Two follow-ups so we don’t paint ourselves into a corner in docs:

A) Naming consistency
Private currently documents the runtime as “Serving Runtime” and uses a `runtimeVersion` field in values.yaml. For LTS should that become:
- `runtime.version: 1.20-lts.1` (string)
- or keep `runtime.version: 1.20.0` style and add `runtime.channel: lts`?

I prefer the first (single field), but want to ensure it aligns with whatever you’re putting in release notes / changelog generator.

B) Upgrade policy text
Can we include a single sentence like:
“Supported upgrades within a given LTS line are monotonic (e.g. 1.20-lts.0 -> 1.20-lts.2). Downgrades are not supported except as part of rollback procedures.”

If yes, I’ll bake that into the Private upgrade doc + installer messages (so the CLI warns on downgrade attempts).

C) Artifact locations (what we can publish)
If we don’t want a moving `1.20-lts` tag, what stable pointer should docs refer to for “find the latest patch”? A web page? A release index? Even a JSON feed?

Today our customers tend to ask “what’s the latest recommended patch” — we should give them a canonical place to look.

Vivek


From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Dec 4, 2025 at 9:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

A) Agree: single field.
Let’s standardize on `1.20-lts.1` as the version string everywhere (release notes, installer, Helm). The branch name can stay `runtime-1.20-lts` internally.

B) Yes on monotonic upgrades.
We should phrase “downgrades not supported” carefully: allow rollback to previous *installed* patch for emergency, but not arbitrary downgrades. Something like:
“Rollback is supported to the immediately previous LTS patch if performed within the same maintenance window and after validating state compatibility.”

(We can refine, but directionally: upgrade forward; rollback one step if needed.)

C) “Latest patch” pointer
We can do this without a moving image tag by publishing a small index in docs:
- Confluence page “Runtime LTS release index” with a table per LTS line (1.20-lts, 1.22-lts, etc) and the current recommended patch.
- Each entry links to release notes, checksums/attestations, and the exact container tag + digest.

Sahana and I can generate this as part of the release pipeline (it can write a JSON blob that docs render). For pilot, we can do manual updates.

If you’re updating the Private guide this week, go with:
- “Refer to the Runtime LTS release index for the current recommended patch.”
- “Pin to explicit patch tag or digest.”

-Connor


From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Dec 4, 2025 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private installer upgrade guidance — align with Runtime LTS versioning + artifact locations

Great — I’ll update Private docs + installer UX to match:

- Version string is `1.20-lts.N` everywhere.
- Upgrade guidance: monotonic upgrades within the LTS line; rollback only to previous patch as part of rollback procedure (wording per Naomi’s guidance).
- No moving `1.20-lts` image tag; instead we point customers to an LTS release index page that lists latest recommended patch + digests + attestations.

Action items:
1) Connor/Sahana: confirm what the “release index” canonical URL/path will be (even if Confluence for pilot).
2) Vivek: update Private installer docs and open a small PR to improve downgrade warning copy.
3) Naomi: sanity check final phrasing for the upgrade/rollback section before we publish.

I’ll send a doc link once edits are in.

Vivek

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
